question: What conspicuity treatment is labeled 'E' in Figure 2A-1?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Item E in Figure 2A-1 is a vertical retroreflective strip on the sign support. The figure illustrates this treatment with a fluorescent yellow-green pedestrian crossing sign assembly whose post carries a matching retroreflective strip extending down the support, ending no more than 2 feet above the ground line. This is one of several optional methods for enhancing the conspicuity of standard signs based on engineering judgment. Options (permitted): - "Based upon engineering judgment, where the improvement of the conspicuity of a standard regulatory, warning, or guide sign is desired, any of the following methods may be used, as appropriate, to enhance the sign's conspicuity (see Figure 2A-1)," with the figure's list of examples including "E - Vertical retroreflective" strip on sign support. Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Figure 2A-1, where item E, labeled "Vertical retroreflective strip on sign support," depicts a fluorescent yellow-green pedestrian crossing (W11-2) sign with a downward diagonal arrow plaque mounted on a post fitted with a matching vertical retroreflective strip that terminates within "2 ft MAX." of the ground line. [Image 5] shows the same Figure 2A-1 in its full-page context (Page 48, Section 2A.11), confirming the "E – Vertical retroreflective strip on sign support" label. Citations: - Figure 2A-1 (p.48) - Section 2A.11 Option §1 (p.49) - Page 89
gold_answer: A vertical retroreflective strip on the sign support.
